title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Picture 58's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0052, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$002D and 0 for channels 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 10 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 3, frame 2 then 2, frame 2 then 1, frame 2 then 6, frame 2 then 1, frame 1 then 12, frame 1 then 2. One pass takes 30 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 12 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 9, frame 4 then 2, frame 4 then 5, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 3, frame 7 then 20, frame 8 then 12, frame 7 then 2, frame 5 then 5, frame 5 then 15, frame 8 then 19, frame 8 then 12. One pass takes 105 steps.

Picture 58's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 43 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 10: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 8 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 5, 6, 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 27 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
Frame 3 of picture 58, named by channel 1's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 4 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 7 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 4, 9 and 10: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 8 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 9 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 6 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 8 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 58, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 7, 11 and 12: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 58's own packed bytes decode to, the 923rd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
